AXLERO SOLUTIONS 
PROJECT DOCUMENT – ADVANCED DATA SCIENCE & ML ENGINEERING 
Real-World Applications - Hands-on System Building 
To continue pushing the boundaries of your Data Science and Machine Learning portfolio into 2026, this 
volume moves beyond standard predictive modeling and time-series forecasting. We focus on the 
bleeding edge of AI research: Agentic Multi-Modal RAG, Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning (PPML), 
and Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning. 
Here are three highly advanced, enterprise-grade ML projects for a senior-level portfolio.

contain complex multimodal data (like financial tables, embedded charts, and images) or when queries

Project 2 - "FedMed": Cross-Silo Federated Learning Engine 
Domain: Privacy-Preserving Machine Learning (PPML) & Healthcare 
Problem Statement: Training highly accurate ML models for rare diseases requires massive patient 
datasets. However, strict data privacy laws (HIPAA/GDPR) prevent hospitals from sharing raw patient 
data with centralized servers. 
Use Case: Researchers at three different global hospitals collaborate to train a brain tumor 
segmentation model using MRI scans. Instead of pooling their private data, they deploy FedMed nodes. 
The central server sends the untrained PyTorch model to each hospital. The models train locally on 
private data, and only the encrypted weight updates are sent back and aggregated (using Secure Multi-
Party Computation) to update the global model, preserving absolute patient privacy.

• 
Federated Learning Framework (Flower / PySyft): Orchestrates the decentralized training loop, 
managing the communication between the central se

preserving absolute patient privacy.

managing the communication between the central server and isolated client nodes. 
• 
Computer Vision Model (PyTorch / MONAI): A 3D U-Net architecture designed specifically for 
segmenting medical imagery (e.g., MRI or CT scans). 
• 
Privacy & Encryption (TenSEAL): Implements Homomorphic Encryption, allowing the central 
server to aggregate the model weights while they remain mathematically encrypted. 
• 
Training Dashboard (React / Recharts): A monitoring UI showing the global model's 
convergence and accuracy metrics across different distributed epochs.

Project 3 - "SwarmRL": Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Simulator 
Domain: Autonomous Systems & Deep Reinforcement Learning 
Problem Statement: Training a single agent to navigate an environment is well understood. However, 
coordinating a swarm of 50 autonomous agents to search a disaster zone dynamically without 
colliding—optimizing their coverage area collectively—is highly complex and fails with standard 
pathfinding algorithms. 
Use Case: A disaster response coordinator uses SwarmRL to deploy simulated searc

lliding—optimizing their coverage area collectively—is highly complex and fails with standard 
pathfinding algorithms. 
Use Case: A disaster response coordinator uses SwarmRL to deploy simulated search drones. The 
backend uses Ray RLlib to run a Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm. The 
agents learn to collaborate in a decentralized manner, sharing spatial rewards to maximize the search 
area covered while heavily penalizing mid-air collisions. The React and WebGL dashboard renders the 
trained swarm executing a flawless, emergent search pattern in a 3D environment.

Key Modules: 
• 
Multi-Agent Environment (PettingZoo / OpenAI Gym): A custom simulated continuous 3D 
space where multiple agents interact, observe their surroundings, and receive localized rewards. 
• 
Reinforcement Learning Engine (Ray RLlib): A highly scalable distributed computing framework 
utilized to train the MAPPO algorithms across multiple CPU cores. 
• 
Deep Neural Networks (PyTorch): The underlying actor-critic networks determining the 
continuous flight paths of the drones based on LiDAR-like state observations. 
• 
3D Simulation UI (React & Three.js): A visualizer that ingests the live model inference 
coordinates and renders the swarm's flight paths and sensor coverage in 3D.
